Welcome

A home for the Faith, built to last generations

Our parish is building a new church, priory, and academy together on one campus. It will be a place where our children and grandchildren can continue the traditional Latin Mass, come to know the Faith, and grow up in a parish family, long after we are gone. We would be grateful to have you with us on the journey.

The Project

One campus for the Mass, the school, and parish life

The Saint Joseph Project is the newest work of the Society of Saint Pius X in the United States. It is one of only a few places in the country where a church, a priory, and an academy are being built together, so that the Mass of All Time, and everything that grows around it, can be handed on here in Post Falls.

We are building in two phases. The first phase gives our parish everything it needs to move to the new land. The second phase is the church itself.

Phase 1 · about $30 million

Moving our parish home

  • Parish hall, which will serve as our temporary church
  • Gym, which will also serve as parish hall and auditorium for now
  • Priory for our priests
  • First academy building
  • Workshop
  • Cemetery and site work

The temporary church will be larger than our current church and designed for the liturgy from the start, a dignified place for Mass, not a makeshift one. The Prior and the Building Committee decide the final order of building.

Phase 2

Immaculate Conception Church

  • The permanent church, designed by McCrery Architects
  • Construction drawings planned for 2029
  • Site preparation planned to begin in 2030

When the church is finished, the parish hall and gym return to their intended uses.

Our Patrons

Under the protection of Saint Joseph and Our Lady

This work is placed in the hands of the two saints who cared for the Holy Family: Saint Joseph, the carpenter who built a home for Our Lord, and the Blessed Virgin Mary in her Immaculate Conception, the patroness of our parish.

Saint Joseph

Guardian of the Redeemer, patron of the universal Church, and patron of workers. A just man who built with his hands and asked nothing for himself. The Guilds, the project, and every stone of the new campus are entrusted to him.

Saint Joseph, patron of the universal Church, pray for us.

The Immaculate Conception

Our parish bears the name of Our Lady, conceived without sin. The new church will be dedicated to her, and the whole campus will stand under her mantle.

O Mary, conceived without sin, pray for us who have recourse to thee.

Tota pulchra es, Maria, et macula originalis non est in te. Thou art all fair, O Mary, and the original stain is not in thee. ANTIPHON FOR THE IMMACULATE CONCEPTION

Become a builder

The Guilds of Saint Joseph

Join the builders

The great churches of Christendom were never built by a few wealthy people. They were built by whole towns: goldsmiths and masons, bakers and farmers, each giving what they could.

Our Guilds carry on that tradition. They are a spiritual fraternity, not just giving levels. Each family joins through a five-year pledge that fits its means, and every Guild is placed under the protection of a patron saint. However large or small your gift, you will be part of this work, and remembered in prayer.

Pledge

What will your family build?

A pledge is a promise to give over five years, in addition to your regular Sunday offering. Spreading it out lets many families give more than they could all at once.

Try a total and a schedule to see what each payment would be and which Guild you would join. When you're ready, you can set it up securely through Tithely. Payments come out automatically, and you'll get an email receipt for every gift.

Circumstances change. If you ever need to adjust your pledge, just call the Church Office at 208-773-7442. No explanation needed.

Questions

Common questions

Where will Mass be said before the new church is built?

In the parish hall, which is being built in Phase 1 as our temporary church. It will be larger than our current church and designed for the liturgy from the start.

What does Phase 1 include?

The parish hall (our temporary church), the gym (which will also serve as a hall and auditorium for now), the priory, a maintenance shop, and our first school building. The current estimate for Phase 1 is about $30 million.

Does Phase 1 depend on selling our current property?

No. Money from the sale is set aside to help with Phase 2 and keep the work moving.

When does the five-year timeline start?

It already has. Schematic design and permitting are the first steps, and they are underway.

What if Phase 2 takes longer than planned?

Even with only Phase 1 finished, the new campus will give us more room than we have today. We will be moving forward, never backward.

How will I know how the money is being used?

Weekly updates in the parish bulletin, plus monthly and quarterly newsletters showing what has been collected and what has been spent.

How are pledges tracked?

Every pledge is recorded under the donor's name in Tithely and the Saint Joseph Project envelope system, so nothing is counted twice.

Who oversees the project?

The Prior leads the project, with a Program Director and three committees: Construction and Design, Fundraising, and Finance. The US District and the General House of the Society provide oversight, so the work continues even if leadership changes.

Can I change my pledge later?

Yes. Call the Church Office at 208-773-7442 and we'll gladly help.

Every gift, large or small, becomes part of a place where souls will be baptized, married, taught, and laid to rest for generations. Give once, give monthly, or give in memory of someone you love. You'll get an email receipt for every gift.

Large gifts by check or wire

For large gifts, a check or wire transfer avoids online processing fees, so the full amount goes to the project.

By check: make it payable to Immaculate Conception Church confirm payee, write "Saint Joseph Project" in the memo, and mail it to 495 N. Lincoln Street, Post Falls, Idaho 83854.

By wire: call the Church Office at 208-773-7442 for wire instructions. For your protection, always confirm wire details by phone. The church will never send changed bank details by email.
